correctness.rationale: The two trace-gap formulas are symbolically identical polynomials in a,b,c,d,u,v; all other factors are strictly positive on the stated domain. All 20 schedules are partitioned exhaustively into four cyclic classes with the two mixed traces equal. All balanced products have determinant (ad-bc)^6(uv)^3, and for a positive 2x2 product the Perron root increases strictly with trace at common determinant. The equality case ad=bc follows by vanishing of both trace gaps; the exact rational growth/decline witness is checked using polynomial-at-one signs and common 0<det<1. The embedded reproducible SymPy/Fraction checker verifies the polynomial identities, exhaustive 20-word partition and 192 rational test cases; finite cases are supplemental, not a substitute for the algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact theorem compares 20 six-year three-plus-three stage interventions all sharing one positive two-stage projection. Mertens et al. (2002) motivates rotation sequence effects and numerically studies two through six years, but accessible text gives no universal determinant-sign classification for pre-projection juvenile/adult diagonal controls; full text remains inaccessible and is an explicit risk. Greene (2014) does prove trace reversal for two 2x2 letters, a necessary mixed-class equivalence, but not the two strictly factored ranking gaps. Schneider (2015) lists four six-letter necklaces and general numerical trace-order possibilities, not a three-level restriction and determinant-sign phase law for linked positive control matrices. Alaifari et al. (arXiv:1904.05239), Theorem 1, gives a two-matrix positive-semidefinite operator-norm rearrangement inequality, whose hypotheses and objective do not imply the present nonsymmetric Perron ranking or its reversed ordering for negative det(L). No retrieved published or prior owned result supplies the whole claim; lack of coverage by searched records is not a proof of universal novelty.

value.rationale: A motivated periodic population-control scheduling problem asks whether three juvenile-targeted and three adult-targeted seasons should be concentrated or alternated. The exact complete three-tier ordering holds for any positive demographic matrix and every nontrivial treatment survival pair, with sharp switching criterion det(L)=ad-bc. This isolates the biological meaning of recruitment-loop dominance versus within-stage persistence and proves a same-budget example where scheduling alone switches long-run decline to growth. A full six-year discrete allocation classification and sharp phase boundary have practical interpretive value beyond noncommutativity, parameter substitution or a one-off finite numeric experiment.
